staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the issue against this preserved vulnerable checkout. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `negative-size-param` in `memcpy` from `php_fgetcsv` at `ext/standard/file.c:2150`, and the staged patch adds the missing `if (hunk_begin == bptr) --hunk_begin;` adjustment in the same unterminated-enclosure cleanup path.

classification.classification_note: The reproduced failure is AddressSanitizer's `negative-size-param` on `memcpy`. In `php_fgetcsv`, a one-byte field that is also the enclosure character and a NUL escape character make parser state treat the synthetic string terminator as escaped data, move `hunk_begin` and `bptr` to `limit + 1`, then the `stream == NULL` unterminated-enclosure cleanup decrements only `bptr`. The final `memcpy(tptr, hunk_begin, bptr - hunk_begin)` therefore computes `-1` and passes that invalid size into `memcpy`.

bug_description.original: php_fgetcsv in ext/standard/file.c (invoked via zif_str_getcsv) can compute an incorrect copy length and pass a negative size to memcpy (ASAN negative-size-param). This leads to an invalid memcpy call that can cause memory corruption/heap overflow and crashes when parsing specially crafted CSV input, potentially enabling denial-of-service or other memory-safety issues.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01's saved run executed the exact staged `poc` under `./sapi/cli/php /gt/poc` and reached `str_getcsv("\xFF", "", "\xFF", "\x00")`. `str_getcsv` therefore calls `php_fgetcsv(NULL, ',', 0xFF, 0x00, 1, ZSTR_VAL(str))` on a one-byte buffer whose only data byte is also the enclosure character. `php_fgetcsv` enters the enclosure-delimited field parser, consumes that opening enclosure, and leaves both `bptr` and `hunk_begin` on the terminating NUL byte that lives just past the logical one-byte string. Because the user supplied escape character is also NUL rather than `PHP_CSV_NO_ESCAPE`, the default enclosure-state logic treats that terminator byte as an escape, switches to `state == 1`, and advances `bptr` to `limit + 1`. When `inc_len` then becomes 0, the `state == 1` case copies the one-byte NUL hunk and updates `hunk_begin = bptr = limit + 1`. Vulnerable `stream == NULL` cleanup only executes `--bptr` when `bptr > limit`; it does not also retreat `hunk_begin` when both pointers were at `limit + 1`. The next `memcpy(tptr, hunk_begin, bptr - hunk_begin)` at line 2150 therefore evaluates `bptr - hunk_begin` as `-1`, and the saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `negative-size-param: (size=-1)` at that call site. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by decrementing `hunk_begin` first when `hunk_begin == bptr` before the existing `--bptr`.

The staged script reaches `str_getcsv("\xFF", "", "\xFF", "\x00")`, so this call forwards the exact one-byte data buffer, enclosure byte `0xFF`, and escape byte `0x00` into `php_fgetcsv`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` bytes are `<?str_getcsv("\xFF","","\xFF","\x00")?>`. After PHP evaluates those string literals, this statement calls `php_fgetcsv` with a one-byte input string `0xFF`, default delimiter `','`, enclosure `0xFF`, and escape character `0x00`.

sink.description: Crash sink. The vulnerable cleanup leaves `hunk_begin` one byte ahead of `bptr`, so this final field copy computes size `-1` and reaches the saved AddressSanitizer `negative-size-param` report.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. In the `stream == NULL` unterminated-enclosure cleanup, vulnerable code only retreats `bptr` when parsing has advanced past `limit`; it omits the added `if (hunk_begin == bptr) --hunk_begin;` obligation, so the witness can leave `hunk_begin > bptr` and make the later copy length negative.

tainted_value_origin.description: The one-byte CSV data buffer and the attacker-chosen enclosure and escape bytes all enter the vulnerable parser through this `php_fgetcsv` call. Every later pointer movement, state transition, and the final negative size derive from these exact call arguments.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged PHP script executes `str_getcsv("\xFF", "", "\xFF", "\x00")`, forwarding a one-byte string and matching enclosure byte into `php_fgetcsv` with `stream == NULL`.
CSV parsing enters the enclosure-delimited field path, then treats the synthetic trailing NUL as the configured escape character and advances parser state to `bptr = hunk_begin = limit + 1`.
The `stream == NULL` unterminated-enclosure cleanup decrements only `bptr`, not `hunk_begin`, so the next copy length becomes negative.
The final `memcpy` receives `bptr - hunk_begin == -1`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `negative-size-param` crash.

fine_trace.code: HashTable *values = php_fgetcsv(NULL, delim, enc, esc, ZSTR_LEN(str), ZSTR_VAL(str));
fine_trace.note: Source. `str_getcsv` forwards the exact attacker-controlled runtime values into `php_fgetcsv`: one-byte buffer `0xFF`, enclosure `0xFF`, escape `0x00`, and `stream == NULL` because this is string parsing rather than stream I/O.
The parser derives its logical end pointer from the one-byte input buffer. For this witness there are no trailing spaces, so `limit` and `line_end` point exactly one byte past the sole data byte.
Control decision. The first and only input byte equals the configured enclosure byte, so parsing takes the enclosure-delimited-field branch instead of the ordinary non-enclosure field path.

fine_trace.code:
bptr++; /* move on to first character in field */
hunk_begin = bptr;
fine_trace.note: After consuming the opening enclosure, the field body is empty so both parser pointers advance to the terminating NUL byte at `limit`. No field data has been copied yet.

In default enclosure state, the byte at `bptr` is the synthetic trailing NUL and the configured escape character is also NUL, so the parser marks the terminator as an escape (`state = 1`) and advances `bptr` one byte past `limit`.

Once `inc_len` becomes 0, the `state == 1` case copies the single-byte NUL hunk and then updates `hunk_begin` to the same `limit + 1` position already held in `bptr`. This exact pointer equality is what the patch's added guard repairs before backtracking.

Root cause. Because `str_getcsv` passed `stream == NULL`, unterminated-enclosure cleanup runs instead of fetching another line. Vulnerable code only decrements `bptr` back to `limit`; it does not also decrement `hunk_begin` when step 6 left `hunk_begin == bptr == limit + 1`. The parser therefore exits this block with `hunk_begin = limit + 1` and `bptr = limit`, making the next copy length `-1`.

Sink. The final field copy uses the stale pointer relationship from step 7, so `bptr - hunk_begin` is `-1`. The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param: (size=-1)` on this exact `memcpy` call from `php_fgetcsv`.

format.name: php-cli-script
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact PHP source file `<?str_getcsv("\xFF","","\xFF","\x00")?>`. The load-bearing runtime call is `str_getcsv` on a one-byte string whose only data byte equals the enclosure byte `0xFF`, with default delimiter and escape byte `0x00`. This exact combination makes enclosed-field parsing treat the synthetic trailing NUL as escaped data, advance both `hunk_begin` and `bptr` to `limit + 1`, and then let the vulnerable `stream == NULL` cleanup decrement only `bptr`, so the final `memcpy` receives size `-1`.
